committee_name.text: Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC), supplemented with members from the Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee

quote.quote: the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) supplemented with members from the Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee, including consumer representatives involved with HIV patient advocacy
This application was discussed at a public advisory committee on May 27, 2010

recommendation.text: The single voting question asked whether the overall risk-benefit of Egrifta 2 mg/day supported approval; all 16 voting members voted yes (16-0), with no abstentions.

quote.quote: All 16 voting members voted 'yes' to this question. There were no abstentions.

linkages.concern: An AC member (Dr. Thomas) raised concern about diabetic retinopathy risk from Egrifta-induced IGF-1 elevations, suggesting a clinical trial with prospective fundoscopic exams.
linkages.change: FDA required a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial in HIV-lipodystrophy patients with T2DM to assess retinopathy risk as a postmarketing requirement.

concern_quote.quote: Noteworthy was a point made by Dr. Thomas on his concerns of diabetic retinopathy (page 260) and that a clinical trial should be conducted to prospectively perform fundoscopic exams of study subjects. Such a proposal has merit and is being discussed with the company as a postmarketing requirement.

linkages.concern: The majority of panel members felt there were inadequate data on whether elevated IGF-1 levels increase malignancy risk, and recommended long-term surveillance, time limits on use, and monitoring.
linkages.change: Panel comments and recommendations were reflected in labeling (monitoring and recommendations for discontinuation of use with persistent IGF-1 increases in the absence of efficacy) and in the applicant's proposed observational study.

concern_quote.quote: The majority of the panel members felt that there were inadequate data to comment on whether elevations in IGF-1 levels would increase risk of malignancies

change_quote.quote: Many of the comments and recommendations from the panel member are reflected in labeling (monitoring and recommendations for discontinuation of use with persistent IGF-1 increases in the absence of efficacy) and the applicant's proposed observational study.

linkages.concern: Several panel members felt there were inadequate data on long-term cardiovascular benefit/risk and recommended a CV outcomes trial.
linkages.change: After the AC, a prospective CV outcomes trial was deemed infeasible; the applicant proposed a prospective observational study collecting MACE events, made a postmarketing requirement.

concern_quote.quote: the majority of the panel members felt that there were inadequate data to comment on long-term CV benefits/risk of Egrifta. Several members recommended a CV outcomes trial

change_quote.quote: The applicant has proposed a prospective observational study that would include collection of MACE events. This would be considered a postmarketing requirement.

summary: A public advisory committee (EMDAC supplemented with Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee members) met on May 27, 2010 and voted unanimously 16-0 that Egrifta's risk-benefit supported approval, heavily influenced by patient testimonials given the absence of other therapies. Committee safety concerns shaped the approval's postmarketing conditions: an AC member's diabetic-retinopathy concern became a required randomized retinopathy clinical trial, and panel concerns about long-term IGF-1/malignancy and cardiovascular risk were addressed through labeling (IGF-1 monitoring and discontinuation guidance) and a postmarketing observational study collecting cancer, hypersensitivity, and MACE outcomes.
